disruptions.name: Carajás / S11D + Serra Norte (Northern System)
disruptions.issue: 2026 guidance cut; Serra Norte licensing and rainfall vs S11D strength
disruptions.evidence: Vale revised 2026 iron ore production guidance down to 335–345 Mt from an earlier 340–360 Mt range. The Northern System's Q1 2026 output at Serra Norte fell 1.2 Mt y/y, reflecting lower run-of-mine availability tied to licensing restrictions and higher rainfall, partly offset by S11D's Q1 2026 record of 19.9 Mt on stronger asset reliability and mobile-equipment utilisation.
disruptions.signal: 2026 guidance: 335–345 Mt, down from 340–360 Mt; Q2 2026 output 84 Mt, +1% y/y.
disruptions.next_checkpoint: Track Serra Norte licensing resolution and H2 2026 rainfall impact against maintained guidance.

source.name: Vale — Production and sales in 1Q26 and 2026

disruptions.name: Iron Bridge
disruptions.status: Ramp-up delayed to FY2028 after impairment
disruptions.issue: Processing-plant erosion and pipeline issues slowed commissioning
disruptions.evidence: Fortescue flagged a non-cash impairment of approximately US$750m pre-tax (~US$525m after-tax) against Iron Bridge's carrying value in its June 2026 quarterly production report, citing premature erosion in the processing plant (requiring ceramic-liner replacement and a redesigned air-based rock-separation step) and a leaky 240km water pipeline from the Canning Basin. Full nameplate production has been pushed back to FY2028.
disruptions.signal: Iron Bridge concentrate shipments: 2.7 Mt for the June 2026 quarter, 9 Mt for FY26 (+27% y/y); FY26 guidance 11–14 Mt versus a 22 Mtpa nameplate, rising to only 16 Mt by FY2028.
disruptions.next_checkpoint: Track port outload capacity upgrades (flagged as the current binding constraint) and whether the FY2028 nameplate timeline holds.

disruptions.name: Pilbara operations (Hamersley, Hope Downs, Robe River, Yandicoogina)
disruptions.issue: Cyclone Narelle and Cyclone Mitchell port closures
disruptions.evidence: Tropical Cyclone Narelle (Category 4) forced closures across Rio Tinto's four Pilbara port terminals from 24 March 2026. Ship loading resumed at East Intercourse Island, Parker Point and Cape Lambert B by 28 March; Cape Lambert A required further repair. Combined with February's Cyclone Mitchell, the two events are estimated to have impacted iron ore shipments by around 8 million tonnes, with roughly half recoverable.
disruptions.signal: 2026 Pilbara shipment guidance maintained at 323–338 Mt despite ~8 Mt of estimated cyclone-related shipment impact.
disruptions.next_checkpoint: Confirm Cape Lambert A repair completion and H1 2026 shipment recovery against the ~4 Mt recoverable estimate.

source.name: Rio Tinto — Iron Ore update following Tropical Cyclone Narelle

tightness.assessment: Supply is broadly loose, though individual signals are mixed. REQ forecasts global iron ore supply growth of about 0.3% a year through to 2031, with most of the rise coming from Guinea, Brazil and Australia. This is a worldwide supply forecast across all producing countries, not a sum of or proxy for the dashboard's tracked mines. Mysteel reports 173.26 Mt at China's 47 major ports on 9 July 2026, down 1.36 Mt (0.8%) week on week; this is China-specific port inventory, not a worldwide stock figure, and is used as the standard proxy for seaborne tightness because China accounts for roughly 70%+ of global seaborne iron ore imports. REQ reports Australian export volumes up 6% year on year in the March quarter. World Steel reports global crude steel output of 1,849.4 Mt in 2025, down 2.0% year on year, while REQ's medium-term outlook has world steel production reaching around 2 billion tonnes by 2031.

indicators.label: Iron ore Capesize freight rates (China-bound)
indicators.signal: Two separate lanes, not one blended figure — Australia's route is roughly a third of Brazil's cost, reflecting the much shorter shipping distance to China. Brazil (Tubarão-Qingdao) rose from $21.35/t (19 Dec 2025) to a two-year high near $37/t in mid-May 2026 — partly driven by a Middle East conflict beginning 28 Feb 2026 that lifted fuel costs and shipping uncertainty — before easing to $33.95/t by 12 Jun 2026. Australia (West Australia-Qingdao, the Baltic Exchange's "C5" route) rose from $10.78/t (21 Nov 2025) to $15.25/t by 22 May 2026, then fell 24.7% in one week to $10.95/t by 12 Jun 2026 — Australia's route has shown sharper week-on-week swings than Brazil's on these data points.

bear.note: Internal downside-demand scenario, not a third-party forecast. The 2025 supply and demand anchor is World Steel Association's 1,633.9 Mt of extra-regional iron ore trade in 2025; using the same observed trade total on both sides keeps the seaborne balance definition consistent. REQ June 2026 supplies the directional premise of rising supply and softening steel demand. Internal extensions: supply grows 2.0% a year (2026: 1,633.9 × 1.020 = 1,666.6 Mt; 2027: 1,666.6 × 1.020 = 1,699.9 Mt), while demand falls 0.5% a year (2026: 1,633.9 × 0.995 = 1,625.7 Mt; 2027: 1,625.7 × 0.995 = 1,617.6 Mt). Rounded to 0.1 Mt.

drivers.assessment: USGS states that almost 98% of iron ore is used in steelmaking. World Steel's 2023 end-use split shows buildings and infrastructure at 52% of finished-steel use. REQ June 2026 expects falling Chinese steel output to be offset by India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, with world steel production reaching around 2 billion tonnes by 2031; the regional rotation supports volume, while rising EAF use changes ore intensity and grade requirements.

methodology.title: 1. Source order
methodology.body: The weekly job checks operator releases, regulatory filings (SEC 6-K, ASX, TSX) and government notices first. It then checks sector and statistical bodies: USGS, World Steel Association, Geoscience Australia and Brazil's ANM. Only after those passes does it query GDELT and broad news for events that may not yet appear in primary disclosures.

methodology.title: 2. Tier definitions
methodology.body: Tier 1 is an operator IR release or regulatory filing — highest confidence, mine/hub-level detail. Tier 2 is a sector or government statistical body — country or segment-level, lower granularity. Tier 3 is news, GDELT, or other secondary reporting, used only to flag events pending primary confirmation.

methodology.title: 3. Weekly-job fit
methodology.body: Every tracked source reports at most quarterly at mine/hub level — there is no genuinely weekly mine-level iron ore disclosure, the same constraint the copper dashboard operates under. The weekly job checks IR pages and filings for new releases (most weeks return nothing) and separately tracks weekly-moving reference series (62% Fe price, freight, China port inventories) so the dashboard stays visibly current between quarterly updates. TODO: those weekly-moving reference series are not yet wired into this dataset.

methodology.title: 4. Outlook discipline
methodology.body: Published forecasts are labelled as such. Internal scenario extensions disclose their assumptions and are never presented as third-party forecasts. Scenario notes must cite "REQ" (Resources and Energy Quarterly, Australia), "IBRAM" (Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração, Brazil) or "internal" — there is no confirmed third-party outlook source for Canada, so Canada-specific assumptions use "internal" until one is found.

methodology.title: 5. Audit trail
methodology.body: Each candidate item records source tier, URL, retrieval time and content fingerprint. Weekly data changes are committed to version control before deployment, giving the team a reproducible history.
